title: POC scoping: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
summary: Initial POC scoping to align success criteria, workload sizing and bench plan. Customer leaning towards Dedicated for predictable latency but has strict security requirements that could push to Private. Action items include sizing spreadsheet, SOC2/network docs, and scheduling benchmark with sample data.
next_steps: Redwood to share Dedicated pricing and burst options
Redwood to send SOC2, architecture and network diagram
Customer to provide sample dataset and representative traffic profile
Schedule benchmark run next week with SE and customer ML engineer
action_items: Lisa Chen - Send Dedicated pricing + committed options - due 2026-05-07
Mark Rivera - Prepare benchmark plan + test script and sizing spreadsheet - due 2026-05-06
Rajiv Kapoor - Provide sample dataset (anonymized) and 2 weeks of traffic logs - due 2026-05-08
Sara Gomez - Share security checklist and questions for Redwood security team - due 2026-05-07
transcript:
00:00 Lisa Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lisa from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Mark my SE is on as well. Nina, thanks for coordinating on your side.
00:12 Nina Patel: Hi Lisa, thanks. We figured we'd use this to scope a POC - understand the success criteria and figure out whether hosted, dedicated or private makes sense for us.
00:21 Mark Rivera: Great. Quick agenda, we'll run through current workload, latency and throughput targets, security constraints, then propose a benchmark plan and timeline. Does that work?
00:30 Nina Patel: Yep. To start, we have two main workloads - realtime triage assistant for clinicians, and nightly batch summarization for records. Real time is small payloads but strict p95 latency under 200ms ideally. Batch can be looser.
00:50 Rajiv Kapoor: Right, realtime sees about 120 qps at peak during daytime, average session length maybe 25 tokens prompt + 150 tokens response. Batch jobs process about 10k records overnight.
01:08 Sara Gomez: From security, we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration for keys, VPC peering or private link, and audit logs retained for 12 months.
01:20 Lisa Chen: Helpful. A few clarifying q's - is PHI stored in your samples? and do you require data residency in the US only?
01:27 Nina Patel: Yes some PHI, so we need HIPAA considerations. US residency is required for primary data, though some subteams may have EU users later.
01:35 Mark Rivera: Understood. So in terms of deployment modes, Hosted gives fastest time-to-value - Redwood hosted API with SOC2 compliance, but multi-tenant. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and better isolation and predictable throughput - helps hitting p95 latency targets at scale. Private (VPC/on-prem) meets strictest network controls but increases onboarding time.
01:55 Tom Lee: Cost is a major concern. If Dedicated is much more expensive, we'll consider caching or quantization first.
02:03 Lisa Chen: Totally, and that's part of the POC - we'll run benchmarks to quantify latency vs cost tradeoffs. Mark will outline the benchmark plan.
02:12 Mark Rivera: Plan idea: 1) runway benchmark on a hosted small instance to validate correctness and pipeline; 2) run dedicated-equivalent sizing with burst and batching to measure p95; 3) run a private deployment if needed for final verification. We'll use a representative sample of your traffic, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1K tokens.
02:36 Rajiv Kapoor: For realtime we need to know how Redwood handles KV cache across sessions and warm start behavior - cold starts kill latency.
02:45 Mark Rivera: Good point. We'll include warmup tests and KV cache hit rates. On Dedicated we can pin model instances to reduce cold starts; hosted also offers some warm pool options but less guaranteed.
02:57 Sara Gomez: On KMS, does Redwood support customer-managed keys or HSM?
03:02 Lisa Chen: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS integrations; hosted can integrate with customer keys for certain enterprise tiers - we'll include exact options in the doc.
03:13 Nina Patel: Timeline - we want pilot validated within three weeks, then a 3 month pilot. Feasible?
03:19 Mark Rivera: For the initial benchmark and sizing, 1 week to run the tests once we get the dataset and traffic profile. For a Private deployment onboarding can take 4-6 weeks depending on network approvals. Dedicated typically 2-3 weeks for capacity provisioning.
03:33 Tom Lee: Who signs off on success? For us product and security both must sign off - product for latency/quality, security for data controls.
03:41 Lisa Chen: Makes sense - we'll capture success criteria as pass/fail metrics: p95 under 200ms for realtime, acceptable quality delta vs your current model (we'll run side-by-side evals), and passing security checklist with KMS and audit logs.
03:54 Rajiv Kapoor: On quality delta - can we run a set of 500 labeled prompts? We need to ensure generation changes aren't regressions.
04:01 Mark Rivera: Absolutely, we'll run eval harness and report BLEU/F1-like metrics or more task-appropriate metrics - also manual spot checks.
04:10 Nina Patel: Also concerned about fallback policies - if load spikes, will we degrade gracefully to a cheaper model or downsample requests?
04:18 Lisa Chen: Redwood supports smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants; we can define canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies to preserve availability. We'll include recommended policies in the proposal.
04:29 Sara Gomez: For audits we'll need network diagrams and where logs are retained.
04:34 Lisa Chen: We'll attach SOC2 report and a network diagram specific to Dedicated and Private options.
04:39 Tom Lee: Any gotchas on inference cost estimation? People often undercount tokens for system prompts and assistants.
04:45 Mark Rivera: We'll include token accounting and an example cost model. Also suggestions: batching for batch jobs, prefix caching for realtime where applicable, and quantized model recommendation if latency/cost balance needs it.
04:59 Nina Patel: Great. Can you also include a recommended Dedicated sizing - like number of GPUs and model variants for our 120 qps?
05:06 Mark Rivera: Yes, we'll run the sizing spreadsheet; preliminary estimate is 4x A100 equivalent for p95 headroom with concurrent sessions assuming 150-token responses, but we'll confirm after benchmark.
05:20 Rajiv Kapoor: Let's schedule benchmark next Tue, does that work for the SE?
05:24 Mark Rivera: Yes I can run it Tue - need the dataset and logs by this Friday to prepare.
05:29 Lisa Chen: Recap: Redwood action items - send pricing, SOC2 and network diagrams, benchmark plan and sizing sheet. Customer action items - provide anonymized sample data and traffic logs, security checklist. We'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark.
05:45 Nina Patel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
05:49 Lisa Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up in email.
05:52 END
